assessment: D2-O5 is awkward: widths overlap between first-attempt and second-attempt partitions, weakening a width-only account. D2-O6 confounds complexity with switching. These competing hypotheses establish neither pilot success nor the cause of missing-part reports.

openings.claim: Layout switching disrupts remembered placement and insertion sequence. Repetition stabilizes that sequence; unfamiliar transitions produce searches or premature insertions even with ordinary-width parts.
openings.delta: Links repetition speed and the width anomaly through sequence interference; customer short-part uncertainty is compatible evidence.
openings.prediction: For the same target layout and prechecked components, attempts immediately following a different layout show more placement corrections and longer insertion time than repeated-layout attempts; a layout-specific sequence cue reduces that transition penalty.
openings.probe: Reuse 12 spare-board samples across both probes. Both workers assemble identical target layouts in counterbalanced repeated and alternating sequences, with and without a handwritten sequence cue. Time selection, insertion, checking and packing separately; count placement corrections and second attempts. Stable troublesome joints would weaken this account.
assumptions: Brief bench trials fit available time without delaying accepted orders.
Existing slips and tools suffice within both cost caps; delivered dimensions, capacity, colors, compartment counts and removable joints remain unchanged.

openings.claim: Unmeasured slot condition or joint alignment creates difficult part-slot pairings despite overlapping partition widths. Repeated three-compartment layouts may encounter fewer such pairings; mixed batches may contain layouts that expose them.
openings.delta: Explains overlapping widths through local joint properties; mixed-batch delay could reflect layout composition.
openings.prediction: Second attempts cluster at particular slots or pairings and persist with correct placement cues, regardless of the preceding layout.
openings.probe: Using the same samples, exchange matched-width partitions among compatible slots and repeat with controlled insertion order, recording pair identity, visible edge condition and attempt number. Counterbalance repetitions to detect wear. Slot-following failures support local slot effects; transition-following failures favor A1.
assumptions: Compatible exchanges preserve the ordered geometry and stationery capacity.
Sample reuse and recording fit the same time and cost envelope; accepted products require no modification.
